title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 253
paragraphs: The male oxen they consider to belong to Epaphus, and on his account they test them in the following manner. If the priest sees a single black hair on the beast, he considers it unclean for sacrifice; and one of the priests appointed for the purpose investigates these matters, both when the beast is standing upright and when it is lying on its back, drawing out its tongue moreover, to see if it is clean with respect to the appointed signs, which I shall describe in another part of this history. He also looks at the hairs of the tail to see if they are growing in the natural manner. If the beast is clean in respect of all these things, he marks it by rolling a piece of papyrus around the horns, and then when he has plastered sealing-earth over it he impresses upon it the seal of his signet-ring, and after that they take the animal away. For anyone who sacrifices a beast that is not sealed, the appointed penalty is death.
